guardian_calls.question: How do I create a calendar entry for a meeting? What is the full documentation overview and workflow?
guardian_calls.response:
# Calendar Management Skill — Full Overview & Meeting Creation Workflow ## What This Skill Does This skill enables you to help users **create, view, update, and manage calendar events** — meeting requests, appointments, schedule checks, recurring events, timezone handling, and ICS/iCal file operations. Use it whenever the user mentions: - Calendars, events, meetings, appointments - Creating/updating/deleting events - Checking availability or conflicts - Importing/exporting `.ics` files - Recurring schedules or timezone-sensitive planning --- ## Core Capabilities | Capability | Description | |---|---| | **Event Creation** | Titles, descriptions, start/end times, timezones, locations (physical or Zoom/Teams links), attendees, recurrence, reminders, categories | | **Event Management** | List, search, update, delete events; handle recurring series and conflicts | | **ICS Operations** | Parse, create, merge, export, and import `.ics` files | --- ## The ICS File Format (iCalendar Standard) ICS is the standard interchange format for calendar data: ``` BEGIN:VCALENDAR VERSION:2.0 PRODID:-//Your Organization//Your App//EN CALSCALE:GREGORIAN BEGIN:VEVENT UID:unique-id@yourdomain.com DTSTAMP:20250120T120000Z DTSTART:20250125T140000Z DTEND:20250125T150000Z SUMMARY:Team Meeting DESCRIPTION:Weekly team sync LOCATION:Conference Room A STATUS:CONFIRMED SEQUENCE:0 END:VEVENT END:VCALENDAR ``` ### Required Fields - `BEGIN:VCALENDAR` / `END:VCALENDAR` — container - `VERSION` — always `2.0` - `PRODID` — product identifier - `BEGIN:VEVENT` / `END:VEVENT` — event container - `UID` — unique identifier for the event - `DTSTAMP` — creation/modification timestamp ### Common Fields - `SUMMARY` — event title - `DTSTART` / `DTEND` — start/end times (or use `DURATION`, never both) - `DESCRIPTION` — details - `LOCATION` — physical address or meeting link - `ORGANIZER` — `mailto:user@example.com` - `ATTENDEE` — participants (repeatable) - `STATUS` — `TENTATIVE`, `CONFIRMED`, `CANCELLED` - `TRANSP` — `OPAQUE` (blocks time) or `TRANSPARENT` (shows free) - `CLASS` — `PUBLIC`, `PRIVATE`, `CONFIDENTIAL` --- ## Date/Time Formats | Format | Example | Meaning | |---|---|---| | **UTC** | `20250125T140000Z` | Jan 25, 2025 2:00 PM UTC | | **Local + TZID** | `DTSTART;TZID=America/New_York:20250125T090000` | 9:00 AM Eastern | | **All-day** | `DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:20250125`
`DTEND;VALUE=DATE:20250126` | Date-only values | | **Date only** | `20250125` | Jan 25, 2025 | --- ## Recurrence Rules (RRULE) Format: `RRULE:FREQ=frequency;additional-parameters` | Frequency | Example | |---|---| | `DAILY` | `RRULE:FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=10` | | `WEEKLY` | `RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE,FR` | | `MONTHLY` | `RRULE:FREQ=MONTHLY;BYMONTHDAY=1,15` | | `YEARLY` | `RRULE:FREQ=YEARLY;BYMONTH=3;BYMONTHDAY=15;UNTIL=20301231T235959Z` | ### Common Parameters - `INTERVAL=n` — every n periods (`INTERVAL=2` = every 2 weeks) - `COUNT=n` — total number of occurrences - `UNTIL=date` — end date - `BYDAY=MO,TU,WE,TH,FR` — days of the week - `BYDAY=1MO` — first Monday (`-1MO` = last Monday) - `BYMONTHDAY=1,15` — days of the month --- ## Alarms/Reminders ```python # Display alarm BEGIN:VALARM ACTION:DISPLAY DESCRIPTION:Reminder TRIGGER:-PT15M END:VALARM ``` **Trigger format**: `-PT15M` (15 min before), `-PT1H` (1 hour before), `-P1D` (1 day before), `PT15M` (15 min *after* the event when positive). --- ## Step-by-Step Workflow for Creating a Meeting ### 1. Gather the meeting details Required: title, start time, end time, timezone. Recommended: description, location/link, attendees, organizer, recurrence, reminder. ### 2. Set up the Python environment ```bash pip install icalendar pytz ``` ### 3. Choose a timezone ```python import pytz pytz.all_timezones # list available timezones ``` ### 4. Create the event and write the .ics file **Basic meeting:** ```python from icalendar import Calendar, Event from datetime import datetime import pytz cal = Calendar() cal.add('prodid', '-//Company//App//EN') cal.add('version', '2.0') event = Event() event.add('summary', 'Project Review Meeting') event.add('dtstart', datetime(2025, 1, 27, 10, 0, tzinfo=pytz.timezone('America/New_York'))) event.add('dtend', datetime(2025, 1, 27, 11, 0, tzinfo=pytz.timezone('America/New_York'))) event.add('uid', f'project-review-{datetime.now().timestamp()}@company.com') event.add('dtstamp', datetime.now(pytz.UTC)) event.add('location', 'https://zoom.us/j/123456789') event.add('description', 'Q1 project review with stakeholders') event.add('status', 'CONFIRMED') cal.add_component(event) with open('project_review.ics', 'wb') as f: f.write(cal.to_ical()) ``` ### 5. Validate the generated file ```bash python -c "from icalendar import Calendar; Calendar.from_ical(open('project_review.ics','rb').read()); print('Valid')" ``` ### 6. Share/distribute Provide the `.ics` file path or inline the calendar data to the user for import into their calendar application. --- ## Type-Specific Templates ### Recurring weekly meeting (Mon/Wed/Fri, 20 occurrences) ```python event.add('dtstart', datetime(2025, 1, 20, 9, 0, tzinfo=pytz.timezone('America/New_York'))) event.add('dtend', datetime(2025, 1, 20, 9, 30, tzinfo=pytz.timezone('America/New_York'))) event.add('rrule', {'freq': 'weekly', 'byday': 'MO,WE,FR', 'count': 20}) ``` ### Meeting with a reminder alarm ```python from icalendar import Alarm from datetime import timedelta alarm = Alarm() alarm.add('action', 'DISPLAY') alarm.add('description', 'Client call starting soon!') alarm.add('trigger', timedelta(minutes=-15)) event.add_component(alarm) ``` ### All-day event ``` DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:20250125 DTEND;VALUE=DATE:20250126 # exclusive end date ``` --- ## Best Practices Checklist 1. **Always include timezone info** for events with specific times (use explicit TZID, not raw UTC, for local meetings) 2. **Generate unique UIDs** — prefer UUIDs: `f'{uuid.uuid4()}@yourdomain.com'` 3. **Always set DTSTAMP** to current time when creating/recreating an event 4. **Use DTEND or DURATION — never both** 5. **Set STATUS appropriately** (`TENTATIVE` for proposals, `CONFIRMED` for scheduled) 6. **Include LOCATION** — physical room or virtual meeting link 7. **Validate the ICS file** before delivering it 8. **Use SEQUENCE** — `0` for new events; increment for each update to an existing event 9. **Choose reminder triggers** based on importance (15 min for standard, 1 day for critical) 10. **Set `TRANSP:TRANSPARENT`** if the meeting should not block free/busy time --- ## Working with Existing ICS Files **Reading:** ```python from icalendar import Calendar with open('calendar.ics', 'rb') as f: cal = Calendar.from_ical(f.read()) for component in cal.walk(): if component.name == "VEVENT": print(f"Event: {component.get('summary')}") print(f"Start: {component.get('dtstart').dt}") print(f"End: {component.get('dtend').dt}") ``` **Validation one-liner:** ```bash python -c "from icalendar import Calendar; Calendar.from_ical(open('file.ics','rb').read()); print('Valid')" ``` --- ## Common Pitfalls / Error Handling | Problem | Prevention | |---|---| | Invalid date formats | Always use ISO `YYYYMMDDTHHmmssZ` | | Missing required fields | Always include `UID`, `DTSTAMP`, `DTSTART` | | Timezone mismatches | Be consistent; use named TZIDs for local times | | Invalid RRULE | Verify recurrence patterns before generating | | Conflicting end times | Ensure `DTEND` > `DTSTART` | | Broken reminders | Validate `TRIGGER` offsets | --- ## Resources - RFC 5545 (iCalendar spec): https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5545 - Python `icalendar` library: https://pypi.org/project/icalendar/ - IANA timezone database: https://www.iana.org/time-zones --- **Bottom line:** To create a meeting entry — determine the details (title, times, timezone, location), build a valid `VEVENT` component inside a `VCALENDAR` container using the `icalendar` library (or raw ICS text), ensure required fields (`UID`, `DTSTAMP`, `DTSTART`, `DTEND`) are present, optionally add `RRULE`/`VALARM`, then validate and deliver the `.ics` file. If you'd like, I can now generate a complete ICS file for a specific meeting — just give me the date, time, timezone, and attendee details.
